reviews.review:
Despite feeling generally unremarkable as a rogue-lite, Roboquest earns its keep by delivering an intense, fast-paced, weapon-switching, high-maneuverable, robot-busting FPS cacophony.

Roboquest's colorful comic book visuals, effective sound design, and s-tier viewmodel animations conspire with the game’s tight movement to create absorbing, high-precision gameplay. Although many of the weapons are ineffective (notably every melee weapon), the variety that's on display is nonetheless impressive. Having that many ways to take down enemies makes those first few hours of picking stuff up just to try it out a joy. Even after getting to know most weapons, I often found myself holding onto unproductive weapon types just because shooting and reloading them is so satisfying. The soundtrack also goes pretty hard.

However, once you're between instances of exhilarating combat, expect to engage with a rather by-the-numbers rogue-lite system. It's not bad. Plenty of fun synergies. A few classes, which vary in usefulness. But the stat-based upgrades often lack creativity and the slow early game makes getting to the meat of a class’s potential slightly tedious. It's also a shame that the permanent upgrades (referred to as gadgets) that meaningfully alter gameplay are tucked discreetly away in a manner that's interesting, but unnecessarily indirect. Combat becomes even more lively once these have been unlocked, so I’d recommend pursuing them asap.

On a different nitpicking note, without the late-game mobility enhancements, the amount of hallways in a standard level can become a problem. As you explore, new enemies are usually dropped in front of you. Since running through enemies in later levels is an easy way to end your run, gameplay (depending on your loadout, gadgets, and the difficulty) can devolve into a choke point peeking cover shooter. Conversely, arena rooms are often too small and low on features that facilitate creative movement. It’s usually easiest to just run in circles around the perimeter since entering the enemy-dense center is bad for your health.

All that said, the outstanding gamefeel at the core of Roboquest undoubtedly outweighs any loose criticism of the rogue-lite or encounter design stuff that I have. The game is an easy recommendation for anyone who is excited by the terms “movement shooter” and “satisfying reloads”.

I'm not really a fan of rogue-lites in generally, but the FPS Rogue-lite subgenre generally offers enjoyable skill-based shooting.  In that aspect, it's very enjoyable.  Neat and creative weapons, lots of enemies with different patterns to figure out.

There are small quibbles I have with it, but some (like the timed aspect that disincentivizes you from exploring) can be turned off, and others are just staples of the genre.  So if you like shooters and you like Rogue-lites, this is a great buy.
